items.title: Ingest I4-I8: v15 overlay, the lost families, siblings, lineage
items.why: The roadmap releases, Appendix-D schemas, worked scenarios, service descriptions and the 30-row canonical domain model come back. Merge is block-level, because 132 v15 files mix real prose with filler and file-level preference would discard real improvements.
items.done_when: Every restored family resolves by ID and the reconciled store reports zero NSV-PRESERVE errors.

items.title: The cross-revision regression report
items.why: Appeared, disappeared, changed-in-place and reappeared, per adjacent revision pair. Reappeared is the strongest signature of accidental loss, and no current tool can see it.
items.done_when: The v14.36 to v15.0 headline reproduces from the real archives and names lost content by identity, not by count. If it does not, the archaeology is wrong.

items.title: nomos-spec-project: profiles and renderers for md, yaml, json, html
items.why: Generated documentation becomes a projection instead of a second source. Five independent barriers stop it becoming source again, because one barrier is a convention and conventions lose.
items.done_when: P3 holds: a rebuild is byte-identical, and building from a fresh import equals building from the original. No timestamp, hostname or absolute path appears in any rendered body.

items.title: Settle how v14 segmented a document carrying a byte order mark
items.why: The v14 decision records carry a BOM and Segment does not strip one, so their front matter is currently treated as content. Every block hash downstream depends on which way v14 read them, and guessing moves hashes the P1-GATE depends on. This gates I4, which ingests records/.
items.done_when: The behaviour is decided against the real v14 files and pinned by a test that fails if it is reversed. If v14's own manifest does not cover a BOM'd document, that is recorded as the reason rather than resolved by preference.

items.title: nomos-capability: the contract registry whose answer is never a bare no
items.why: A capability nobody registered must answer Unknown, not No. Collapsing those is how 'we cannot tell whether this rule applies' becomes 'this rule does not apply', which is the same defect as a validator that never ran. The registry is also the seam every provider and every check resolves through, so it exists before either.
items.done_when: An unregistered capability yields Unknown and a registered-but-unavailable one yields a distinct answer naming why. A test asserts the two are not the same value and that no code path turns either into a grant.

items.title: nomos-analysis: FactIdentity, FactReader, FactStore and invalidation
items.why: The load-bearing architectural bet, still untested. FactIdentity is the cache key AND the identity, one type, so a fact cannot be reused under a key that does not describe it. FactReader is the only read path and records a dependency edge on every read, which is what makes invalidation dependency-complete rather than hopeful.
items.done_when: A change in any one of FactIdentity's components invalidates, asserted component by component rather than in aggregate. Require() returns the honest degraded Applicability on failure and never a fabricated fact. Reading through FactReader records an edge; a test proves a read that recorded no edge is not possible.

items.title: nomos-lang-rust: recognition and syntax facts from syn
items.why: The first thing in this repository that reads somebody else's code. A provider with a declared Guarantee, so that what it can and cannot answer is a value rather than an assumption a check makes about it.
items.done_when: Syntax facts over real files from F:/repos/xvpe, with the provider's Guarantee declared and asserted to match what it actually produces. A file it cannot parse yields Unparseable, never zero findings.

items.title: The vertical slice: real facts over the real xvpe corpus
items.why: Answers whether any of this works before more of it is built. Three checks the prototype learned the hard way: a rule firing thousands of times is background hum, a check that found zero findings corpus-wide was broken rather than satisfied, and a negative control that has never failed is not a control.
items.done_when: Facts materialize over F:/repos/xvpe's Rust files. A second run materializes zero. Touching one file recomputes exactly its descendants and no more, asserted by naming them rather than by counting. Every number reported comes with what it was measured over.

items.title: nomos-store: content-addressed documents with one write door per authority
items.why: Observed facts and authored specification never share a store. The snapshot document is the only door in, so nothing can write a fact by another route and leave the index describing something that was never recorded.
items.done_when: A snapshot written and reread is byte-identical, and the derived index is rebuildable from the documents alone — proven by deleting it and rebuilding to an identical state.

items.title: nomos-workspace: snapshots, build variants and the single change door
items.why: Every change source — correction, IDE edit, git checkout, agent edit, code generator — enters through one WorkspaceChangeSet and produces one new generation. A second path would be a second answer to what the workspace currently is.
items.done_when: A portable snapshot over F:/repos/xvpe is interpretable by a process with no access to that tree, and 100 ingestion-order permutations yield byte-identical queries.

items.title: Table rows as typed subjects: content and separator
items.why: A block already guarantees byte completeness, so rows are not what makes a document reconstructible. Rows exist so a loss report can name what went missing by identity — the MetricTradeoffProjection row — rather than by count, which is the plan's own stated bar. Typing them keeps 282 and 258 as two queries over one table instead of one number bent to match the other.
items.done_when: Every pipe line in a table block is stored as a typed row. Over the six v14 domain volumes the store answers 282 pipe lines and 258 content rows, both measured rather than asserted. Exactly one separator per table is enforced, so a content row cannot be mistyped out of NSV-PRESERVE-002's view. The bundle exporter carries the new table and P1 byte identity still holds.

items.title: Read the versioned archives without unpacking them
items.why: About twenty archives hold every revision. Reading them in memory keeps the corpus out of the working tree, so nothing can mistake an extracted revision for authored source — which is the same barrier that stops generated output becoming source.
items.done_when: Every archive opens and its entries are addressable by path without writing to disk. An archive that cannot be read is an error naming which one, never an empty listing that reads as an archive containing nothing.

items.title: I4: the v15.0 overlay, merged block by block
items.why: 132 v15 files mix real prose with filler, so file-level preference would discard real v15 improvements along with the filler. Each filler paragraph is ingested as derived authority with a regression-filler lineage row pointing at the v14 block it displaced. Stubs are evidence, not rubbish.
items.done_when: The 363 requirement, 169 story and 157 acceptance identifiers reconcile against v14 hashes, reported per identifier and never summarised. Every filler block carries a lineage row naming what it displaced, and the 64 records that exist only in v15 are ingested as new authored nodes.

items.title: I5: restore the families v15.0 destroyed
items.why: The 8 roadmap releases, Appendix-D schemas and profiles, 8 worked scenarios, Appendix-H telemetry, 54 service descriptions, the E.1 headless inventory, F.1 IDE profiles and the glossary. Section 5's canonical domain model comes back as one table block plus a concept node per row, each with a lineage row to its originating row — one canonical source, two projections, never two authorities.
items.done_when: Every restored family resolves by identifier and the reconciled store reports zero NSV-PRESERVE errors over a non-zero subject count. The 30 domain models resolve individually, named, not counted.

items.title: I6 and I8: sibling suites, and the game plans as lineage
items.why: The XVPE, KWB and ecosystem seeds enter as non-root suites, so a cross-suite relation is an ordinary row rather than a special case. The game plans enter as commentary authority under D-120: lineage, never sole authority, and a rule enforces that rather than a convention asking people to remember it.
items.done_when: Sibling suites carry authority_root=0 and their schemas resolve as nodes. Every game-plan block is commentary authority, and a test asserts no normative statement traces to one as its only source.

items.title: I7: revision fingerprints across every archive
items.why: Appeared, disappeared, changed in place, and reappeared. Reappeared is the strongest signature of accidental loss and no existing tool can see it, because a file tree cannot tell a deletion from a reorganisation.
items.done_when: Every adjacent revision pair yields the four sets. Counts carry the unit and the corpus they were measured over: 282 pipe lines of which 258 carry content, and 3 code blocks over the six domain volumes, with the plan's 6 recorded as a fence count rather than silently corrected.
